# Google Colab: Complete Notebook and Chapter Notebooks {.unnumbered}

In addition to the web edition and PDF, the book provides **two complementary ways to work in Google Colab**:

1. a **complete master notebook** with the general book workflow in one file;
2. **14 independent, self-contained chapter notebooks**, designed so that a reader can study or practice one topic without running previous chapters.

::: {.callout-tip title="Recommended access"}

**Index of chapter notebooks:**  
[Open the Colab notebook index](https://colab.research.google.com/github/gilbertorodriguez59/libro-machine-learning-r/blob/main/colab/00-indice-colabs.ipynb)

**Complete master notebook:**  
[Open the complete book in Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/gilbertorodriguez59/libro-machine-learning-r/blob/main/Aprendizaje_y_Clasificacion_Automatica_con_R_Colab.ipynb)

:::

## What does self-contained mean? {.unnumbered}

Each chapter notebook includes the preparation needed for its topic. Depending on the chapter it can:

- install the required R packages;
- create working folders;
- download the prepared data used in the examples;
- verify that resources exist;
- set random seeds for reproducibility;
- load packages and helper functions before analysis.

This means that a student can open **SVM**, **Random Forest**, or the **Chapter 14 integrated benchmark** and begin directly from that notebook.

::: {.callout-warning title="Run cells in order within each notebook"}
Although chapter notebooks are independent from one another, some cells inside a notebook depend on objects created earlier in that notebook. If Colab restarts the session, run again from the first cell.
:::

## Complete master notebook {.unnumbered}

The master notebook preserves the integrated book workflow in a single file. It is useful for studying the book from beginning to end, keeping a complete copy of the R code, comparing algorithms in one session, and retaining the ATUS and COVID-19 examples.

For classroom work, exercises, and quick consultation, the chapter notebooks are usually more convenient.

## How to work in Google Colab {.unnumbered}

1. Open the index or the chapter you want to study.
2. Sign in with a Google account if Colab requests it.
3. Optionally choose **File → Save a copy in Drive**.
4. Verify that the runtime uses **R**.
5. Run the setup cell first.
6. Continue in order using the play button or `Shift + Enter`.

## Web book, Colab, and interactive laboratories {.unnumbered}

The web edition remains the primary option for reading, navigation, and Shinylive laboratories. Colab notebooks are designed for changing code, repeating experiments, and working with R models without installing R or RStudio locally.

**Chapter 14** includes a dedicated notebook for running the common seven-classifier comparison under the same training, validation, and test partition.
